# Universal Volunteer Core

> **Current release: owner-authorized, AI-reviewed reading guidance.** This edition was reconciled from campaign-supplied source material. It is not an independent human audit, legal advice, staff appointment or fieldwork authorization.

> **Current operating status:** use the volunteer portal for passkey accounts, reading, orientation, role preferences and practice worksheets. Regulated activities, campaign calling tools, staff operations, private incident submissions and donations are not activated by this release. Never collect supporter data or money, use scraped lists, autodial or send mass texts. Private preview links and passwords are for authorized review; do not distribute them as public campaign links.

> **Before acting:** the current activity module, jurisdiction, training, two distinct verifiers, publication approval and approved tools must all match. A guide, a completed orientation, a worksheet or a saved role preference never substitutes for that authorization.

*Read this before taking any public campaign action.*

A self-service operating manual for truthful, lawful, safe, and useful volunteer work in a decentralized independent presidential campaign.

> **For:** Every volunteer, organizer, host, captain, creative contributor, and campaign supporter

> **Status:** Campaign proposal and volunteer guidance. Verify changing law and campaign instructions before regulated activity.

## Start here: the volunteer operating system

> **The one rule:** Tell the truth, protect people, and use only lawful methods. If a tactic depends on changing law, money, private data, automation, a permit, or an official campaign account, pause until the required verification exists.

This campaign is volunteer-built. That means you are trusted to act without waiting for a supervisor on ordinary, low-risk work—and expected to stop when a legal or safety boundary appears. The standard is not whether a tactic is clever. The standard is whether a reasonable person could verify what you did, whom you contacted, what you said, and whether consent was respected.

| Lane | You may do | What changes the lane |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Green — act now | Share official public links; talk with people you know; host a small discussion; print unaltered official material; invite people to the official volunteer account. | No private data collection, spending, automation, or claim of campaign authority. |
| Yellow — use the campaign system | Canvass, call, text, table, run an event, recruit, or submit creative work using an official list, script, form, and approved asset. | Use the current instructions; honor opt-outs; record only the requested minimum. |
| Red — stop and verify | Petition circulation, voter registration, paid media, mass calls/texts, contracts, fundraising custody, permits, data exports, public statements for the campaign. | A current state module, written authorization, or legal review is required. |

> **No supervisor available?:** A missing answer never turns a red-lane action green. Choose a green-lane action, document the unresolved question through the official volunteer form, and continue with work that cannot harm the campaign.

## The campaign in one page

Justice for All begins with protecting rights, identifying actual harm and repairing it without creating another injustice. An unrepaired public wrong can leave continuing losses; the proposed remedy must address the people actually harmed and protect others' rights.

The current three-issue platform is Kirk–Evers, The Garden and The Cornerstone. Use their current campaign pages and the matching reading guides. Other September 2026 policy kits are historical references and are not launch positions in this release.

Every policy remains a proposal unless a current authoritative source establishes otherwise. Do not promise eligibility, a legal entitlement, an enacted program, a benefit or a guaranteed outcome.

## Your first 60 minutes

1. Read this core and the packet for the role you want to perform.
2. Open the current campaign website directly and confirm that the material you plan to share matches the current official platform.
3. Choose one measurable action small enough to finish today: five practice messages without recipients or personal details, one public post, one practice event plan without an attendance list, or one issue conversation.
4. Use the supplied script as a starting point, then speak in your own ordinary voice. Do not add statistics or promises you cannot source.
5. Send people to the current official site form rather than recording their private information yourself.
6. Log the activity through the current official volunteer form if one is available; otherwise keep only anonymous totals and do not retain names or contact details.
7. Choose the next action and schedule it on your own calendar.

- [ ] I know which role packet applies.
- [ ] I can state that the platform is a proposal.
- [ ] I know my stop conditions.
- [ ] I have not created a private contact database.
- [ ] My next action has a number and a date.

## Truth, attribution, and message discipline

- Quote only words that appear in the current official platform, and keep enough context that the meaning is not distorted.
- For summaries, say ‘the campaign proposes’ or ‘the platform would.’ Distinguish the campaign’s argument from independently established fact.
- Use dated, primary sources for factual claims. If you cannot retrieve the source, remove the number rather than guessing.
- Never fabricate endorsements, poll results, ballot status, staffing, partnerships, scientific readiness, costs, savings, or legal authority.
- Do not present AI-generated text, images, audio, or video as a real person, event, endorsement, or campaign statement.
- Do not alter an official graphic in a way that changes its claim, disclaimer, date, or context.
- If speaking personally, say so. Do not use a title that implies authority to bind the campaign.

| If asked… | Say… |
| --- | --- |
| Is this official? | I’m a volunteer sharing the campaign’s published material. The current official position is at the current campaign website. |
| Can you promise this will happen? | No. It is a governing proposal that would require legislation, implementation, and public oversight. |
| What does it cost? | The platform describes repayment and portfolio rules, but I won’t invent a score. Independent scoring and implementation details would be required. |
| Is the candidate on my ballot? | Ballot access is state-specific and still must be verified. Please check your state election authority and the campaign’s current status. |

## Respectful persuasion

A useful conversation is not a contest. Ask permission, learn what the person cares about, offer one relevant idea, check understanding, and leave the relationship intact.

1. Open: ‘May I tell you about one idea from an independent presidential campaign?’
2. Ask: ‘What problem do you most want the next president to solve?’
3. Reflect: summarize their concern without arguing with it.
4. Connect: explain one proposal in no more than two sentences.
5. Check: ‘What part sounds promising or unclear?’
6. Answer only what you know. Use ‘I don’t know’ freely and point to the official platform.
7. Invite one next step: read or practice using the current volunteer portal.
8. Thank them and end promptly if they decline.

> **De-escalation:** If someone becomes hostile: lower your voice, do not crowd them, do not touch them or their property, say ‘I’m going to end the conversation now,’ and leave. Call emergency services for immediate danger. Online, save evidence only if needed, block/report, and do not mobilize followers against the person.

## Privacy and digital security

- [ ] Use a unique password and multifactor authentication on every campaign-related account.
- [ ] Open campaign pages by typing the official domain; be cautious with login links sent by strangers.
- [ ] Collect supporter information only through the current official form. Never photograph sign-in sheets or copy data into a personal spreadsheet.
- [ ] Do not collect Social Security numbers, dates of birth, government IDs, full voter files, medical information, payment information, or immigration status.
- [ ] Do not upload supporter data, call lists, internal documents, or private conversations to a public AI tool.
- [ ] Share files as view-only unless editing is necessary; remove access when the task ends.
- [ ] Keep minors’ information out of personal devices and never arrange one-on-one unsupervised activity with a minor.
- [ ] If a device or account may be compromised, stop using it for campaign work, change credentials from a trusted device, and report through the official volunteer form.

> **Data minimization:** If the official campaign form is unavailable, distribute public information and count outcomes anonymously. Do not build a substitute contact list.

## Money, materials, and legal boundaries

- Unpaid personal volunteer services are generally not contributions under federal campaign-finance law, but money, goods, paid promotion, facilities, transportation for others, or professional work can create a contribution or reporting issue.
- Use the official donation form. Do not accept cash, checks, card numbers, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or donor login credentials.
- Never reimburse yourself, promise reimbursement, pool money, sign a contract, rent space, buy a list, or order materials in the campaign’s name without written authorization.
- Do not use an employer’s staff, equipment, paid time, postage, mailing list, or facilities for campaign activity. Incidental-use rules are technical; the simple campaign rule is to use your own device and your own time.
- Do not buy or boost political ads. Unpaid personal internet activity is different from paid placement.
- Do not imply that campaign contributions are tax-deductible. Do not run a raffle, lottery, auction, or prize promotion without written legal clearance.
- Foreign nationals may face restrictions on political spending and decision-making. No one should contribute or direct campaign strategy unless federal law permits it.
- Place the campaign disclaimer on official public communications when supplied. Never crop, cover, or shrink it beyond legibility.

> **Internal no-spend rule:** Assume personal spending is not authorized and will not be reimbursed. Ordinary personal internet access and truly incidental activity are fine; anything beyond that belongs in the stop-and-verify lane.

## Calling, texting, and automation

A group of volunteers may hold a social call-bank gathering. Calls must be placed by real people, one at a time, using a lawful campaign-provided list and current script, or by volunteers contacting people they personally know. A call-bank party does not authorize automated dialing, prerecorded audio, artificial voice, or mass messaging.

| Allowed with the stated condition | Not allowed under this library release |
| --- | --- |
| A volunteer manually calls one number, identifies the campaign, speaks live, and records the requested outcome. | Autodialers, predictive dialers, prerecorded calls, ringless voicemail, artificial or cloned voices. |
| A volunteer sends a personal message to someone they know and respects a decline. | Bulk texts, purchased/scraped numbers, repeated messaging after opt-out, or tools that disguise sender identity. |
| A group uses one current campaign script and immediately updates do-not-contact status. | Importing campaign lists into personal apps, sharing screenshots, or keeping a duplicate contact database. |

> **Universal opt-out:** If someone says stop, do not contact them again through that channel. Mark the opt-out immediately in the official system. If no official system is available, end the contact and do not retain or reuse the number.

## Safety, inclusion, and conduct

- Follow venue rules, public-access rules, permit conditions, and lawful instructions from election or public-safety officials.
- Never threaten, intimidate, stalk, harass, dox, discriminate, obstruct access, damage property, or interfere with another campaign’s event or materials.
- Never carry a weapon while volunteering, even where lawful, and never volunteer while impaired.
- Use a buddy system for canvassing, petitioning, late events, and unfamiliar locations. Share a check-in plan; leave any place that feels unsafe.
- Offer accessible routes, seating, captions or transcripts, readable type, and a way to participate without standing or speaking publicly.
- Do not pressure anyone for political support in exchange for help, services, food, employment, housing, rides, or access.
- Do not use slurs or speculate about a person’s race, ancestry, disability, religion, citizenship, gender, medical history, or criminal history.

> **Emergency rule:** For immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911 or the appropriate local emergency number. Campaign reporting never replaces emergency services.

## Self-service decision tree

| Question | If yes | If no |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Could this action change someone’s legal rights, ballot eligibility, donation record, or contact consent? | Use the current official process; stop if it does not exist. | Continue. |
| Does it involve money, a contract, paid reach, private data, automation, a permit, or an official account? | Written authorization or an activated campaign tool is required. | Continue. |
| Am I certain the claim appears in the current platform or a cited primary source? | Use accurate context and date. | Remove the claim or say you do not know. |
| Could a reasonable person think I speak for or can bind the campaign? | Identify yourself as a volunteer and narrow the statement. | Continue. |
| Is anyone unsafe, pressured, impaired, or asking to be left alone? | Stop immediately and protect safety/consent. | Proceed respectfully. |

## Measure work without collecting people

The campaign needs enough information to learn, not enough to surveil. Unless the official campaign system requests more, record anonymous totals only.

| Record | Do not record |
| --- | --- |
| Date, role, general area, minutes volunteered, number attempted, number reached, number interested, number directed to official form, common question, safety/compliance issue. | Political opinions tied to names, screenshots of private messages, medical or immigration information, payment details, unverified allegations, or a shadow supporter list. |

A useful debrief is three lines: What happened? What did I learn? What will I change next time? Submit it through the current official volunteer form when available.

## Official references

Rules change. Use the current official page at the time of action.

- [FEC: Volunteer activity](https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/candidate-taking-receipts/volunteer-activity/)
- [FEC: Advertising and disclaimers](https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/advertising-and-disclaimers/)
- [FEC: Who can and cannot contribute](https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/candidate-taking-receipts/who-can-and-cant-contribute/)
- [FCC: Political robocalls and robotexts](https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/political-campaign-robocalls-and-robotexts-rules)
- [U.S. EAC: Register and vote in your state](https://www.eac.gov/voters/register-and-vote-in-your-state)

## What success looks like

- One accurate, permission-based explanation you can practice without collecting people
- No bulk spam and no private database
- A clear invitation to read, volunteer, or donate through the official site

> **Your 60-minute start:** Choose one current issue and rehearse a general explanation without writing names, contact details or individual political concerns. Use only released public material in any later consent-based conversation.

## Set up the action

1. Do not make a private contact list, use scraped contacts or buy a list.
2. Do not write down or infer another person’s political concerns, preferences or sensitive traits.
3. Read one current issue page and prepare a source-based explanation without profiling a person.
4. Send individual messages at a humane pace. Personalize; do not paste a wall of text.
5. Record anonymous totals only.

## Words you can use

Opening script

> **Say this in your own voice:** Hi [first name]—I’ve been reading Phillip Galinsky’s independent 2028 platform. One idea on [issue] made me think of our conversation about [shared concern]. Would you be open to a short link? No pressure at all.

Follow-up script

> **Offer one next step:** Thanks for taking a look. What landed for you, and what felt unclear? I’m a volunteer, so if I don’t know an answer I’ll point you to the campaign’s published platform rather than guess.

Scripts are guardrails, not a performance. Keep required identification and legal language exact; otherwise sound like yourself.

## Run the action

1. Review the legal, safety, consent, and privacy checks before the first contact.
2. Begin with the smallest useful batch so errors are cheap to correct.
3. Ask permission and give the other person an easy exit.
4. Use only current official links, forms, lists, scripts, and unaltered materials.
5. Record only the requested result; honor opt-outs immediately.
6. Stop on any red-lane condition.
7. Debrief in three lines and choose the next action.

- [ ] Identity was clear.
- [ ] Consent was respected.
- [ ] Claims stayed within published material.
- [ ] No private list or unauthorized spending was created.
- [ ] The next volunteer can understand the handoff.

## When something goes wrong

| Situation | Response |
| --- | --- |
| They do not reply | Do nothing. Silence is not consent to repeated messages. |
| They disagree | Ask one curious question, reflect their answer, and end warmly. |
| They want updates | Direct them to the current official signup form; do not add them to your own list. |
| They ask you to debate publicly | Choose a respectful one-to-one exchange or decline. Do not dogpile. |

## Stop conditions

> **Do not proceed:** Stop, preserve safety and evidence where appropriate, and switch to a green-lane action if any condition below applies.

- Sending the same unsolicited message at scale
- Contacting someone after an opt-out
- Using employer/customer/member data
- Promising access, favors, benefits, or policy outcomes

## Quality scorecard

| Measure | Good | Warning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accuracy | Every factual claim is in current campaign material or a dated primary source. | A number, quote, status, or promise cannot be verified. |
| Consent | People can decline easily; opt-outs are immediate. | Repeated contact, pressure, or hidden recording. |
| Privacy | Official forms handle personal information; local notes are anonymous. | Names, contact data, screenshots, or exports on personal devices. |
| Completion | One action, one owner, one deadline, one anonymous result. | Vague activity without a finish line or handoff. |

## Freedom is not a reward for agreeing with the government.

Speech and democratic participation give the American people the power to correct their government. Those protections must hold when an opinion is unpopular, a challenger is inconvenient, or the people in power would rather not be questioned.

Kirk–Evers brings a single principle to that problem: no government should use coercion, retaliation, or manipulation to silence lawful political participation.

01

02

### Make rights enforceable.

Why Kirk–Evers?

The name honors Charlie Kirk and Medgar Evers across different eras and beliefs. The principle is that no one should face political violence for advocating their convictions.

- Viewpoint-neutral protection

- Lawful speech and participation

Visit The Cornerstone ↗CONCEPT ILLUSTRATIONThe principleHow it worksQuestionsFull frameworkCAMPAIGN PROPOSAL

WHY IT MATTERS

## A public decision should not leave a private debt unpaid.

An industry can change for many reasons. The Cornerstone addresses a narrower problem: identifiable workers whose lawful livelihoods are deliberately destroyed or materially contracted by government action.

The remedy would be a productive replacement opportunity owned and governed by the affected workers. It is not a promise to restore every old job or a guarantee that a new business will succeed.


THE MECHANISM

## What would change.
01

### Establish the injury.

Use evidence and fixed certification rules to connect a government action to the workers and livelihoods actually harmed.
02

### Let workers organize.

Eligible workers form voluntary associations, with equal founding ownership and one-member-one-vote control.
03

### Negotiate what comes next.

Associations negotiate new commercial opportunities with participating states. Training and startup support help turn an opportunity into an operating enterprise.

QUESTIONS WORTH ASKING

## Details matter.
Does every displaced worker qualify?

No. The proposal uses a defined government-action trigger, evidence of causation, and certification. A research census entry is not an eligibility determination.
Would outside funding take control away from workers?

Worker control is central. The design separates an economic return from governing power; a public surplus share does not itself buy a vote, board seat, or management authority.
Is a successful business guaranteed?

No. The remedy is an enforceable opportunity, not a guaranteed profit. Commercial feasibility, training, transparent rules, and independent safeguards still matter.

## The current message

Justice for All means protecting rights, identifying actual harm and repairing it without creating another injustice. Focus on the current three issue pages: Kirk–Evers, The Garden and The Cornerstone. The wider five-pillar September source outline and the fifteen other historical policy kits are not additional launch positions in this edition.

## Four parts of an accurate explanation

1. Name a specific problem without stereotyping a group.
2. Say “the campaign proposes” and explain only the mechanism found in the current source.
3. Name a safeguard and a real unresolved question.
4. Offer a single appropriate next step: read, practice or ask a source-based question. Contributions are not open.

## Keep claim levels distinct

An observed fact needs a current primary source, date and scope. A campaign interpretation is attributed to the campaign. A proposal uses future-tense language. A projection names its assumptions. A personal view is presented as your own. A study does not establish endorsement and a proposal is not an enacted entitlement.

## Practice wording

“May I explain one proposal and the question I think it still needs to answer? The campaign proposes [mechanism from the current issue page] to address [specific harm]. Its safeguard is [published safeguard]. I do not know [unresolved detail], and I will not promise an outcome.”

Do not attribute the temporary YouTube clip to a finished candidate issue presentation. Do not publish drafts or circulate private preview credentials as official public campaign material.

## Correction procedure

Stop repeating an unsupported claim. Find the exact current source. Correct the same audience and channel as visibly as practical, stating what was wrong and what the source supports. Keep a source reference and a version; do not attack the person who identified the error. Use the local Correction worksheet for public-source wording, without private narratives or identifying information.

## Before sharing anything

- Identify yourself accurately and obtain consent for a conversation.
- Verify every number, quotation, legal status and claimed endorsement.
- Keep draft/publication status, rights, disclaimers, alt text and captions clear.
- Do not use sensitive personal data, bot amplification, deceptive media or mass messaging.
- Check that a real public campaign destination has been released; the current private preview is for authorized review.
